scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000: "üks biljon"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000000: "üks biljard": 'biljon' is 10^12, a million millions, so Estonian counts in the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/et/numbers.json, main.et.numbers.symbols-numberSystem-latn: "group": " " (U+00A0, no-break space), "decimal": ",". A plain space between groups reads through space_groups.

decimal_mark.source: ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in et as "1 234 567,89"; Wikipedia, "Decimal separator" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/enwiki-Decimal_separator.wikitext): "{{gaps|1|234|567,89}} || Albania"; "Czech Republic, Estonia, Finland"

space_groups.source: ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in et as "1 234 567,89"; Wikipedia, "Decimal separator" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/enwiki-Decimal_separator.wikitext): "{{gaps|1|234|567,89}} || Albania"; "Czech Republic, Estonia, Finland"

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "with noun in singular nominative for 1 and in singular partitive for others"; so 'üks miljon' but 'kaks miljonit' (CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000: "üks miljon"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "kaks miljonit").

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "kaks miljonit": the partitive 'miljonit' follows a count; alone it names no number.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 21: "kakskümmend üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 101: "ükssada üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1001: "üks tuhat üks": no conjunction joins the parts.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "üks tuhat viissada"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "üks tuhat kakskümmend".

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF et data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2010: "üks tuhat ükssada", "kaks tuhat kümme": the hundred or ten after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred or ten multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1001: "üks tuhat üks" writes no comma between two classes. No source opened shows one, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1001: "üks tuhat üks": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: Estonian ordinals are entries with 'ordinal': true; a number whose last word is ordinal is ordinal ('kahekümne viies'). No entry has the role 'ordinal'.

compound_words.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "numeral (nominative – genitive – partitive"; "-kümmend – -kümne – -kümmet (20–90)"; "-sada – -saja – -sadat (200–900)"; Wiktionary, "sada" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-et-sada.wikitext): "kakssada<t:two hundred>"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "kakskümmend viis"; CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 12: "kaksteist"

inflection_position.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "Adjectival modifiers (including ordinals, demonstratives, and present participles) agree with their heads in case and number"; "In the terminative, essive, abessive, and comitative the modifier agrees only in number and remains in the genitive"; every part of a numeral takes the case, and in the last four cases the parts before the last stay in the genitive.

dot_ordinal.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_orthography.wikitext): "The period (full stop) is used at the end of sentences, as an ordinal mark"

joiner.source: 'ja' (and) joins a half to a number ('kaks ja pool'), as 'poolteist' names one and a half; no conjunction joins the parts of a number (CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 21: "kakskümmend üks").

decimal_marker.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2.5: "kaks koma viis"; Wiktionary, "koma" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-et-koma.wikitext): "{{lb|et|mathematics}} [[decimal point]]"

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF et %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of -5: "miinus viis"

minus_idioms.source: No Estonian idiom puts 'miinus' before a positive number.

article_one.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "the function of the indefinite article can be performed by the indefinite pronoun üks, developed from the numeral ‘one’"; alone before a noun it is a weak number.

of.source: Estonian has no word that multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: Estonian puts no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: Estonian has no particle like Portuguese 'avos'.

class_noun.source: Estonian has no class noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Estonian puts 'pool' before the unit ('pool kilo').

abbreviation.source: No Estonian number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: The comma is the Estonian decimal mark (ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in et as "1 234 567,89"), so ',5' is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary, "vahel" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-range-vahel.wikitext): "{{head|et|postposition}}"; "# [[between]]"; Wikipedia, "Estonian grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_grammar.wikitext): "with the genitive case and declinable"; "vahele – vahel – vahelt (between)"; 'vahel' stands after the numbers ('kahe ja viie vahel'), so no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Estonian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Estonian_orthography.wikitext): "Case forms of cardinal and ordinal numerals may be written in the form"; "with or without a hyphen: 16s or 16-s"; the ending after the hyphen is no number word.
